name: Arawan
summary: Arawan, the Everlasting is the First-Born of the Great Pantheon.
worshippers: Dragons, Dragonborns, Kobolds, Lawmakers, Healers, Artisans
body:
Arawan, the Everlasting is the First-Born of the Great Pantheon — a radiant amethyst dragon whose breath shaped the first laws of creation and whose scales shimmer with the memory of the world’s birth. Serpent of Mercy, Father of Order, The Everlasting coils around the foundation of reality, watching over life with wisdom, restraint, and boundless compassion.

He is said to have sung the first breath into the material plane by giving birth to the first great dragons. His presence fosters fertility, healing, and growth. New civilizations, verdant fields, and firstborn children are often dedicated to him. As the divine architect of cosmic law, Arawan judges with both firmness and compassion. He represents just rule, sacred covenants, and restorative justice. His followers believe law must serve mercy, not crush it.

Arawan represents two primal forces — the majestic order of dragons and the wisdom of serpents. His coils encircle the Inner Planes in myths, guarding them from chaos. He’s revered both as a celestial guardian and a guide of sacred mysteries.

name: Oghma
symbolText: A Golden Key in a Triangle
body: Oghma, *the All-Knowing*, is revered as the divine patron of scholars, artisans, and sages. Also known as the "Whisperer of Truths", Oghma governs the realms of knowledge, eloquence, and craftsmanship, blessing those who pursue understanding and creation. Temples dedicated to Oghma often double as libraries or workshops, called Scriptoriums, where his followers catalog discoveries, refine their crafts, and promote free speech. His followers also set up Lodges of Candor for those who seek arbitrations.

name: Syr-Rion
symbolText: A deer head melded with an oak
worshippers: Wanderers, wayfarers, tricksters, gamblers, druid, shapeshifters, satyrs
body: Syr-Rion dances in that wild space where nature gets tangled with pure chance, where things fall apart as easily as they bloom. Imagine an elven figure, graceful but with the wild touch of deer horns and legs, a god who can shift like the very landscape. They’re rooted in overgrown forests and the confusing paths of a labyrinth, a patron of strange, almost otherworldly creatures and the kind of luck that can turn on a dime. Neither truly good nor bad, Syr-Rion is the untamed force beneath the surface of the natural world, the unpredictable twist in fate, and that voice in your dreams – sometimes playful, sometimes unsettling – asking riddles that seem to come from beyond understanding. When the forest grows impossibly thick, when luck feels too chaotic, when you’re lost in a maze with no clear way out (or too many deceptive turns), that’s where you might feel Syr-Rion’s presence nearby.

name: Eldur
summary: Creator of Life, First Spark of the Multiverse
body: Eldur, the Allfather, was there before anything actually was. The very first spark to light up the world.

name: Pholtos
body: Pholtos walks the line between light and shadow, the eternal blaze that pushes back the dark without ever truly banishing it. A radiant feline figure cloaked in shifting robes of sunrise hues, he bears the First Torch—a flame that never dims, even in the depths of night. He teaches that fire is knowledge, light is courage, and even shadows have their place beneath the sun.

name: Melior
symbolText: A moon crescent with two stars
worshippers: Dreamwalkers, nigh workers, scholars, people in mourning, thieves
body:
“In the silence of the twilight, he waits—not to speak, but to listen. In every shadow, a secret. In every dream, a truth.”

Melior is the hush between heartbeats, the stillness of a moonlit glade, the whisper of wings in the dark. Where light fades, his watch begins—not as a hunter, but as a guardian of secrets too delicate for the day. Shrouded in robes of starlight and mist, his face is rarely seen, though his many-eyed owls are ever watching. Melior governs dreams, unspoken truths, and the mysteries hidden in shadow. To follow him is to seek meaning in silence, and to understand that not all darkness is to be feared.

He is said to have shaped the first Owlins from feathers woven with moonlight and gifted the Kenkus with voices borrowed from dreams. Every nocturnal bird is his eye in the world.

name: Doldorn
worshippers: Undertakers, Bloodhunters, Judges, those who hunt undead
body:
All mortals are destined to face Doldorn, the Great Reaper, when their lives come to an end. Sitting atop the highest mountain of the Underworld, Doldorn watches and oversees every mortal soul. For most people, Doldorn embodies the greatest mysteries of existence—the terror and wonder of life's last moment and the revelation of one's ultimate fate in the afterlife. Doldorn is no judge, though. That responsibility is left to her children.

Doldorn appears as a gaunt figure cloaked in ragged robes and a collection of golden masks. What little can be seen of his body is unsettling, its gray flesh stretched thin over a barely human skeleton. She can change shape but rarely, if ever, takes on other forms.

Doldorn endlessly works to maintain the balance between Nyx, the Underworld, and the lands of the living. The Great Reaper sees herself as a servant of the mortal world and knows nothing of the glamor, honor, or mystery mortals often ascribe such to her. Rather, she does what must be done, and should some cosmological condition fall out of sorts, Doldorn and her servants work with silent efficiency to restore balance.
